item.title: Rules are meant to be broken
item.description: Wildlife filmmaking has one sacred rule, never interfere, and a BBC crew in Antarctica looked at fifty freezing penguins and decided some rules deserve to be broken. The Dynasties penguin rescue (2018) is one of the most debated and beloved moments in nature documentary history, the emperor penguin episode of David Attenborough's BBC series capturing the day a film crew chose compassion over protocol. The mood is the observer's oath cracking under the weight of conscience. At Atka Bay, where director Will Lawson, cinematographer Lindsay McCrae, and camera assistant Stefan Christmann endured 337 days of temperatures plunging toward minus sixty, a blizzard drove a group of mothers and chicks into a steep icy gully, cut off from the colony, some chicks already lost to the cold, and the crew filmed through heartbreak as the survivors slid back down the slick walls attempt after attempt. Two agonizing days later came the decision that made history: intervening passively, never touching a single bird, they dug a shallow stepped ramp into the ice and simply walked away, leaving the choice to the penguins, and the footage of the colony waddling up those hand-carved stairs to safety became one of television's most tearful triumphs. Attenborough noted on air how rare such intervention is, and executive producer Mike Gunton later revealed the legend himself said he would have done exactly the same. This is documentary storytelling confronting its own ethics, and answering with a shovel. What makes it a must-see is the debate it settled. Objectivity matters, but when saving lives costs nothing and harms nothing, humanity is allowed to pick up the spade

item.title: My weight loss milestone
item.description:
July 2026
July 2026
June 2016
September 2018
September 2024 I've been working with a dietician and have been on a "weight loss journey" for quite awhile, currently down from 320 to 190 as of today. I can officially fit my entire body into one pant leg from jeans I wore religiously in 2024. I can also now fit in a medium size unisex tee. I'm in my mid 40s and I haven't been this small since I was 18. Cutting out sweets along with staying in a calorie deficit and exercising has been successful for me. I didn't really have anyone to share my exciting news with, so I figured I'd share with you all lol.
